Commentary.Commentary: 211. New Zealand will now look to bat just once and fast in this game. The light was fading a bit and it might get worse in the third session. Let us hope for the play to go on as long as possible as the players sip on a cup of tea before they come back for the final session of play. Join us for that in a bit...

The innings began beautifully for the away side, with Tamim Iqbal and Shadman Islam stitching a 75-run stand. Post that though, there was nothing of any significance. Wagner was introduced after 30 overs of the innings but provided immediate impact. The short ball barrage continued from where it left off in the first Test and the Bangladesh batsmen threw their wickets. No partnerships down the order meant the innings folded at a sorry total in terms of the start they got. Wagner picked up 4 wickets, while Boult picked up 3. The other 3 pacers had 1 each to their credit. Kane Williamson would have surely taken this at the toss, to bowl out the opposition in a couple of sessions means there is still hope for a result in this Test that saw a couple of days being washed out.

What a stunning turnaround this has been from the hosts! Bangladesh have been bowled out for 211 after being 119/1 at one stage. In fact, the last 4 wickets were lost for 5 runs. Neil Wagner was the star once more, starting the damage while Trent Boult came back in the end to wipe off the tail. Mahmudullah said at the toss that they will have to be careful not to repeat the mistake of throwing away the chance to score big in the first innings after getting a start, but that is exactly what has happened here.

OUT! Full and straight! You miss, I hit stuff from Trent Boult. Ends with three wickets. The yorker from Boult, Jayed charges down the ground to hit that ball but fails to make contact and the stumps are disturbed. Bangladesh are bowled out for 211! IT WILL ALSO BE TEA ON DAY 3!
On a good length on off, Jayed defends it off the back foot.
Bowls a yorker on middle, Jayed does well to dig it out.
FOUR! Good shot. Full on middle, Jayed drives it straight past the bowler through mid off for a boundary.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Jayed looks to play the upper cut but misses it.
Fuller one on middle from Boult, Jayed defends it back to the bowler.
Almost the end of the innings! A peach outside off from Southee, shaping away late in the end. The ball goes past the outside edge as Hossain looked to defend.
Ebadot Hossain is the last man in.

OUT! Nine down! A length ball outside off, Liton Das tries to come outside the line of the ball and then play it past the slips for a single down to third man but all he can do is to hit it in the air and straight to Kane Williamson at gully. He is not dropping those. Southee has his first wicket. Bangladesh have lost their last three wickets for one run.
On off, Das taps it to point.
Length delivery on off, Liton plays it to point.
On a good length and outside off, Liton lets it go.
WIDE! On a good length and outside off, Das leaves it alone. Umpire signals wide for height.
Short of a length delivery, Das pulls it towards mid-wicket.
Abu Jayed is the new batsman in.

OUT! Timberrrr! That was a brainfade moment from Mustafizur there. A length ball on the off stump line from Boult, Rahman leaves the ball and watches in bewilderment as the ball goes striaght on to knock the off stump in front of his eyes. He is in shock there as to how the stumps have been disturbed. Maybe he took a wrong guard or expected the ball to swing away or to bounce more, no one will know but Boult is surely happy there. Second wicket for him in the over.
Fuller one on the pads, Mustafizur looks to flick but the ball goes off the pads towards short leg. No appeal for LBW as the ball was outside the line.
Mustafizur Rahman walks in next at number 9.

OUT! Three reds and Taijul has to continue walking as the on-field decision will remain. Boult has his first! A fuller length ball landing on middle and going on straight with the angle. Taijul looks to flick it away through the leg side but misses the ball and gets hit on the pads in front of the stumps. The appeal follows and so does the finger. The batsman after consulting his partner takes the review but the replays show that the ball was hitting leg stump. Islam also takes a review along with him. 3 left now for New Zealand to wrap up this innings.

Review time... Taijul has been adjudged LBW to Boult but he has taken this upstairs. Does not look like there was any bat on it. Only the ball missing leg stump can save him. Let's see what the replays have to say...
Bouncer on middle! Taijul looks to duck under the ball but is on the floor as he got so low.
Fuller outside off, some away movement in the air. Taijul survives and drives towards cover.
On the pads, worked away to deep square leg for a run by Liton Das.
On a good length and outside off, Taijul offers no shot.
On a good length and outside off, Islam looks to swing at this one but misses it.
Bowls a bouncer, Islam does well to duck under it.
Short delivery again, Das pulls it towards square leg for a run.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Short of a length delivery, Das pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
A good length ball on top of off stump, Das stands tall and defends it off his back foot.
A good solid defense to end the over from Taijul. Maiden from Boult on his return.
Short one outside off, kept off watchfully from within the crease.
Short of a length and Taijul looks to pull that ball but fails to put bat on ball.
Bouncer outside off, TI ducks under the ball and lets it go.
Fuller one outside off, pushed back towards the bowler.
On a good length and carries really well to the keeper after it is left alone outside off by Taijul.
Trent Boult is back into the attack.
On a good length on off, Liton keeps it out.
Full on off, Das drives it to mid off.
NO BALL! Too many bouncers in the over. 200 up for Bangladesh. Bowls a bouncer, Liton ducks underneath it. The umpire gives Southee a warning.
On a length on off, Das guides it to third man.
Length delivery on off, Das plays it to point.
Bowls a bouncer, Liton does well to duck under it.

The physio is out in the middle to check Liton's finger. Das looked to be in some pain but seems to be fine to continue. Meanwhile, the umpires are discussing the light issue again. The light glasses are out but the on-field umpires have told the fourth umpire not to come on yet with the light-reading machine.
On a good length on off, Das defends off the back foot and he gets hit on the glove. He is in pain.
The umpires had a chat in the middle of overs, and came together to check the light. They feel it is okay right now for play to continue...
WIDE! Bowls it down the leg side, Das leaves it alone.

Drops just short again! Short length ball on the pads of Taijul, he looks to pull it but the ball goes uppishly and without timing towards square. Raval comes inward trying to take that catch but the ball does not have enough on it to carry to diving Jeet. Lucky for Islam.
On a good length on off, Islam looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards first slip where it fell short of the fielder.
Bowls a bouncer, Islam does well to duck under it.
Length delivery on middle, Islam flicks it to mid-wicket.
On a good length on middle, Taijul flicks it to the leg side.
Bowls it down the leg side, Islam lets it go.
Bowls it down the leg side, Das lets it go.
Length delivery on off, Islam plays it towards point for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Islam plays it to covers.
Bouncer! The southpaw ducks in time to let that one go over him.

Just short of Taylor! A short length ball to the right-hander from around the wicket by Southee at the ribs. Liton looks to pull but is not in control, almost hitting it to short fine leg. The ball though dips on Ross there and he makes a half stop diving to his left, allows for a single to be taken.
Short of a length delivery, Islam looks to pull but gets a top edge. It goes towards third man for a single.
FOUR! That is a good shot! A short length ball from around the wicket to the right-hander, Das gets outside the line by moving away from leg stump. He hits it through point for a boundary.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Another short length ball on the leg stump line, Islam looks to do the same thing as the previous ball but fails to put bat on ball.

That is a brilliant take down the leg side! It is followed by a big appeal but the umpire is unmoved. The ball has come off the sides of the batsman. A short length ball on the leg stump line, Taijul looks to come inside the line and glance it fine but misses the ball and gets hit on the hip. The ball goes to the right of Watling who dives and takes the ball superbly, almost colliding with Kane Williamson at short fine leg. An appeal follows but a good decision is made by the umpire.
Bouncer on middle! The batsman looks to pull it away but the extra bounce on that ball takes it over the head of the batsman.
Short of a length on the leg stump line, Liton drops his hand as he plays that ball. It goes off the outside edge through the slips for a single down to third man.
Outside off, Taijul does not bother to play at that.
On a good length on middle, Islam keeps it out.
FOUR! On a good length on off, Islam looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes wide of second slip for a boundary.
Short and outside off, Islam looks to cut but misses it.
On a good length on off, Islam defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on middle, Das nudges it towards square leg for a run.
Tim Southee is now into the attack.
Short one on top of middle stump, dabbed down to third man for a single by Das as he retains strike for the next over.
Another bouncer on middle, well left by Das as he ducks under the ball.
Bouncer on middle, Liton ducks under the ball and lets it go through to the keeper.
Shorter one on the hips, glanced down to fine leg for a single by TI. The ball goes to the right of short fine leg who was positioned there for exactly that shot.
Short length ball on middle, Taijul stands tall and defends the ball back down the ground.
Bowls this one down the leg side, Taijul looks to run it down fine but fails to put bat on ball.

TOP EDGE BUT SAFE! Short of a length delivery, Das looks to pull but gets a top edge. It goes towards square leg where there is no fielder positioned there. The batsmen pick up a couple. Big over for Bangladesh. 14 runs have come from it.
Length delivery on off, Das plays it to point.
FOUR! Third boundary of the over. On a good length on off, Das looks to defend but it goes of the outer half of the bat towards third man for a boundary.
On a good length on off, Das defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Liton Das. This was even better. Full and outside off again, Das drives it through covers again for a boundary.
FOUR! Cracking shot. Full and outside off, Das drives it through covers for a boundary.
On a length on middle, defended by Islam onto the surface.

Drinks break! In the hour since Lunch, 3 wickets have fallen and all of them have been lost to poor shots off short pitch bowling, completely unnecessary. Soumya Sarkar, Tamim Iqbal and Mahmudullah are all back in the pavillion. Liton Das is the last recognised batsman left in the middle and will look to do something alone with the new batsman who has joined him in the middle, Taijul Ahmed. The hosts, on the other hand, will look to wrap up the tail quickly.

OUT! Wagner has his fourth! Mahmudullah who was hopping around and defending the short balls so far has finally become prey to the short ball. He looks really disappointed but the fact is he will have to go. A short length ball on top of middle, Mahmudullah looks to come inside the line and to pull it on the toes. He tries to play the ball along the ground but the ball goes off the leading edge and in the air towards de Grandhomme at square leg who picks up a dolly. Number 4 for Wagner and number 6 for New Zealand. This is some special stuff from the left-arm fast bowler!
Length delivery on off, the skipper plays it to point.
On a good length on middle, Mahmudullah keeps it out.
On a good length on off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a good length on off, Das guides it towards third man for a run.
Beaten outside off! A length ball with some away shape on it through the air. Mahmudullah comes ahead and looks to defend but ends up playing inside the line.
FOUR! Short of a length outside off, nice width available for the batsman and Mahmudullah makes full use of it. He cuts it beautifully through backward point for a boundary.
A solid defense from the batsman to this length ball on top of off stump.
Pushed towards point by Mahmudullah.

Short of a length outside off, played towards point. The non-striker backed up a long way and the point fielder throws the ball at the bowler's end. Boult who was moved to mid on backs up but fails to stop the ball again. No overthrow though. A laugh for all the fielders there.
FOUR! Nice shot. Poor fielding by Trent Boult at covers. Full toss outside off, Mahmudullah drives it through covers where Boult lets it go through him for a boundary.
Dabbed down to point by Liton. The point fielder is a little deep and the batsmen think of a single but decide against it in the end, wisely.
Short of a length on middle, Das looks to come outside the line and then hit it over slips but fails to put bat on ball.

Ouch! Bouncer hits the helmet and goes towards the leg side. Short on middle, Mahmudullah is late to react to the ball and before he can sway or duck, the ball pings off the helmet and goes to the leg side. The batsmen pick up a single and the umpire gives it as a leg bye. On replays, we hear two noises that suggest to us that the ball might have gone off the glove before going on to hit the grill.
Bouncer on middle, the batsman stands on his toes and keeps it down towards short leg once more.
On a short length once more aimed at the hips, Mahmudullah looks to work it on the leg side but plays it straight at short leg.
Shorter length ball on middle, Mahmudullah takes his bottom hand off the bat and defends this towards short leg.
Length delivery on off, Das plays it to point.
On a good length on middle, Das keeps it out.
Full on middle, Mahmudullah drives it towards mid on for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but misses it.
On a good length on off, the skipper defends it off the back foot.
Full on middle, Mahmudullah defends it out.
On a length and top of middle stump, defended back towards the bowler by LD.
Follows up with another bouncer does Wagner, left alone properly this time by Liton.

Ouch! Hit on the grill! A bouncer on middle, Das drops his hands and looks to sway out of the way. The ball though is really quick and gets him on the helmet before rolling to the keeper. The bowlers and the fielders ask the batsman if he is okay, he responds with a thumbs up.
Bouncer on leg stump line, Das ducks under the ball and lets it go.
Well defended by Liton off the back foot to this short ball on middle stump line.
Shorter one on the middle stump line, Mahmudullah pulls it away but was not it total control of the ball. He manages to get it in the gap to deep square leg for a run.
On a good length on off, Das blocks it off his front foot.

LOUD APPEAL FOR LBW! Not out says the umpire. On a good length on middle and leg, Das looks to defend but gets hit on the back thigh pad due to the inward movement on this one. Henry appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Hawk Eye shows that it is going over the stumps. Good decision.
On a good length on off, Das keeps it out.
On a good length on off, Das defends it off the front foot.
On a good length and outside off, Das shoulders his arms to this one.
FOUR! Liton Das is off the mark with a boundary. Full on off, Das drives it through covers for a boundary.

Appeal for caught behind from the keeper and the short leg fielder but turned down by the umpire. A short one on the leg stump line, Mahmudullah looks to duck and leave the ball but the ball seems to have brushed something while going through to Watling. It is the arm guard signals the umpire and the New Zealand keeper too feels the same. They decide not to go upstairs.
A solid defense off the back foot from Mahmudullah.
On a good length on off, Mahmudullah rises on his toes and defends it off the back foot.
On a good length and outside off, Mahmudullah offers no shot.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Mahmudullah tries to get away from the ball.
On a good length on middle, the skipper defends it off the back foot.
Kane Williamson is off the field meanwhile...
On a length and outside off stump, pushed towards the point fielder to end a successful over for Henry.
Liton defends this coming slightly ahead.
A length ball on top of off stump, played towards the point fielder by Das.
Liton Das walks in to bat next.

OUT! This is poor, poor cricket from Soumya Sarkar and Bangladesh. Absolutely unacceptable in Tests. A length ball on top of off stump from Henry, good pace 138 clicks that one. Soumya without any foot movement looks to pull it away but gets a top edge and the ball just goes high in the air and nowhere else. Watling settles under the ball and takes a comfortable catch, his third of the innings. That is an awful shot. Half the side is back in the hut now for Bangladesh. They are 152/5 from 119/1.
Full on off, the skipper drives it towards covers for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but gets beaten due to the away movement on this one.
Bouncer on middle, Soumya ducks under the ball and lets it go through.
Outside off this time and played with soft hands towards the point fielder by SS.
Just like in the previous over, Sarkar comes inside the line to a short ball on leg stump line and looks to hit it over fine leg but makes no contact.
Slightly short of a good length on middle, Soumya defends it towards point.
Aimed at the hips of Mahmudullah, he works it away to deep square leg for a run.

Edgy! Only one slip there and a length ball outside off takes the outside edge of Sarkar as he looked to run it down to third man. The batsmen take a single. Would have been out if there was a second slip. The single brings up the 150 for the visitors.
Length delivery on off, the skipper plays it to point.
On a good length again on middle, Mahmudullah looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a good length on off, Mahmudullah defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on leg, Sarkar nudges it towards the leg side for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Sarkar looks to guide but gets beaten on this one.

SIX! What a shot! Right back over the bowler and into the sightscreen. A fuller length ball on middle, Soumya hits it with a straight bat and nonchalantly right into the sightscreen. Huge! The bowler is not impressed.
Shorter outside off, guided down to third man for a single by Soumya for a single as he keeps strike.

Bouncer on the leg stump line, the southpaw looks to glance it away on the leg side but the ball narrowly misses his glove and goes through to the keeper. There is a stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire.
Short of a length again on middle, good bounce on it. Soumya looks to come inside the line and then hit over fine leg but fails to put bat on ball.
Bouncer on middle, Sarkar ducks under the ball and lets it go through.
Slightly short of a good length from Wagner on the hips of Soumya, the batsman looks to glance it down on the leg side but the ball goes off the hip and towards the keeper who dives to stop the ball.
Short of a length at the hips, Mahmudullah goes deep in his crease and works it towards square leg for a run.
On a good length on off, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Outside off, Sarkar shoulders his arms to this one.
FOUR! Nice shot. Length delivery on off, Sarkar guides it towards third man for a boundary.
Length delivery on off, Sarkar plays it through point. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Outside off, Sarkar does not bother to play at it.
On a good length on off,Sarkar defends it off the back foot.
Short one again to end the over, above middle stump. Mahmudullah goes back in his crease and defends that ball well.

Aimed at the ribs this time, fended uncomfortably by the batsman. In fact, Mahmudullah had taken his eyes off the ball at the time of contact. The ball luckily for him, goes off the glove and towards the off side of the surface.
A short one as expected to welcome Mahmudullah, he stands tall and defends the ball.
Mahmudullah walks in at number 6. These two had a big partnership in the last game, can they do it here?

OUT! Wagner has done it again! Oh Bangladesh! what are you doing? Short of a length on middle, Tamim looks to pull this stylishly but the ball goes off the top edge and high in the air. It goes only as far as short fine leg where Southee from a leg gully position comes and settles under the ball and takes it easily. Tamim after doing all the hard work has thrown it away. Bangladesh once again are falling to the short ball ploy. Wagner has three now.
Short of a length and aimed at the hips, Soumya comes inside the line of the ball and works it away to deep backward square leg for a run.
A short ball on top of middle, Tamim stands on his toes and pats the ball towards the off side. The batsmen pick up a quick single.
Neil Wagner to bowl from the other end. Or should we say continue the short stuff?
On a good length on off, the batsman blocks it off his front foot.
Bowls a yorker on off, Sarkar manages to dig it out.
FOUR! First ball boundary for Sarkar. On a good length on off, Sarkar looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes wide of the second slip fielder towards third man for a boundary.
Full on middle, Iqbal drives it towards mid on for a run.
We see Neil Wagner doing his stretches... looks like he will continue from the other end.
Full again on off, Tamim drives it to mid off.
Full on off, Tamim drives it to covers.

We are back after Lunch. The players and umpires are out in the middle, New Zealand players are in a huddle. Tamim Iqbal is joined by Soumya Sarkar in the middle. Matt Henry will start the proceedings after Lunch.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Thus, in the end, what could have been Bangladesh's session outright ends up being slightly less in favour of them. New Zealand will want to come back after Lunch and continue picking up wickets quickly. Meanwhile, the away side will hope someone can partner Tamim and build a good stand. Back in about 40 minutes for the resumption...

After being inserted to bat by the Kiwi skipper Kane Williamson on a green top, the Bangladeshi openers did really well to score 74 runs in the first period of play before drinks. They batted together for more than 20 overs but post the break, the stand was broken by Colin de Grandhomme who got Shadman to knick one behind to slip. Tamim though continued in his merry ways and made yet another fifty, being positive all along. Mominul who joined him looked comfortable at the crease. All that changed though when Neil Wagner was finally introduced into the attack. He went to the previous match tactic of short-pitched bowling and it paid immediate dividends. He picked up the two wickets of Mominul and Mithun both who knicked behind to Watling. Tamim meanwhile is at the other end and has looked really good so far.

What an absorbing end to a brilliant session! A great session in terms of runs scored for Bangladesh as 127 were made. It has been spoiled right at the end due to the loss of wickets. Three have fallen when at one stage it looked like the away side would head into the break at the loss of just one wicket. The session though has belonged to Tamim Iqbal and towards the end, Neil Wagner.

OUT! Is this deja-vu or what? Just like Mominul, Mithun also goes after the very next ball post changing an out decision to not out. Another short length ball from Wagner, this time outside off, Mithun looks to defend it initially with an angled bat but looked in two minds in the end as he tried to leave it. The ball takes the under edge and goes to the keeper who makes no mistake. Wagner is pumped up once more, New Zealand have picked up two quick wickets and they have three for the session after a poor start. A maiden-wicket over to end the session. LUNCH ON DAY 3!

NOT OUT! That has indeed gone off the arm guard. The Hot Spot does not show much but the replays and Snicko show us there was a deflection off the arm guard. A short length ball aimed at the ribs, Mithun looks to get inside the line and pull it on the leg side but the ball goes to the keeper after taking a deflection. The umpire raises his finger immediately. The batsman in reaction reacts immediately. The replays roll in and show that the arm guard touched the ball and not the glove or the bat. Hence the on-field decision is overruled. The only question there would be wouldn't it have been out if the arm guard was touching the glove.
Mithun like Mominul before him has reviewed after being caught by the keeper. It was an immediate review, but it seemed out to the naked eye. The batsman feels it has gone off the elbow guard.
A short one aimed perfectly at the ribs of Mithun, he defends uncomfortably. The ball goes towards the short leg fielder.
Bouncer once more on the leg stump line, Mithun ducks under at the last moment and leaves the ball.
Another shorter one on the middle stump line now, Mohammand jumps and fends it off towards the off side.
Shorter one down the leg side from Wagner, Mithun moves out of the way and lets the ball go.
On a good length on off, Tamim blocks it off his front foot.
On a good length and outside off, Iqbal shoulders his arms to this one.
Bowls a bouncer, Tamim does well to duck under it.
Length delivery on middle, Mithun flicks it towards square leg for a run.
On a good length on off, Tamim keeps it out.
FOUR! Nice shot. Short of a length delivery, Iqbal rises on his toes and lofts it over third man for a boundary.
On a length on middle, Mithun looks to defend the ball but gets it off the inside half and the ball rolls towards deep square leg. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Bowls a bumper, Mithun does well to duck under it.
On a good length on middle first up to the new batsman, Mithun defends it off the back foot.
Mohammad Mithun walks in next.

OUT! He survived by the review last ball, but is gone this time though! Caught down the leg side off the glove! A short of a length ball landing on middle and going down leg with the angle. Mominul looks to leave that ball but the ball takes the glove on its way to Watling who pouches that ball easily. This time, Haque walks off knowing he has got that off his glove. Wagner is pumped up. Why not, New Zealand has just got their second wicket.

NOT OUT! The ball has gone off the shoulder. The Hot Spot as well as the Snicko tell the third umpire that the ball has not hit the bat and had hit the body. A short of a length delivery outside off, Mominul looks to defend the ball but the ball moves away and he seems to have got an outside edge to the keeper. There was a certain noise and all the fielders celebrate. The umpire too nods his head. The batsman though reviews immediately. The replays roll in and confirm indeed that the ball did not get bat at all. Mominul survives.
Reviewed by the batsman as he is adjudged caught behind. Mominul thinks that the ball has come off the shoulder. He went up immediately.
On a good length and outside off, Haque lets it go.
Length ball on the pads, turned towards square leg for a single by Mominul. He keeps strike.
Third short ball on a trot, Haque gets low under it. Hamilton anyone?
Another bouncer on middle, MH ducks under the ball this time.
A bouncer from Southee, Mominul sways out of the way.

FOUR! Taylor has just touched the rope while trying to pull the ball inside. A length ball outside off from Southee, and a genuine outside edge of Mominul is induced. The ball goes between the slips and gully. Ross gives chase and tries to pull the ball in but makes contact with the rope the same time he pulled the ball in.
Outside off, Haque offers no shot.
On a good length and outside off, Tamim looks to cut but gets beaten on this one. 10 runs off Wagner's first over.
FOUR! What a shot from Tamim Iqbal. Full on off, Iqbal drives it through covers for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle, Haque flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, Mominul offers no shot.
FOUR! Good shot. On a length and outside off, Haque guides it towards third man for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Iqbal flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Neil Wagner is into the attack for the first time this morning, after 30 overs.
On a good length on off, Iqbal defends it off the back foot.
Short delivery outside off, Iqbal plays it towards gully.
On a good length and outside off, Iqbal looks to chase this one but misses it.
On a length outside off, defended into the ground by Tamim.

FOUR! Just wide and then goes all the way for a boundary! A short ball outside off, Tamim pulls it towards mid on with a flat bat but is not in control. Wagner at a widish mid on dives to his right but goes for the catch with his left hand as he is worried about his right hand that he injured earlier while fielding. The ball beats him and goes to the fence. That boundary also brings up the 100 for Bangladesh.
On a good length and outside off, Iqbal shoulders his arms to this one.
Full on middle, Haque flicks it through mid-wicket. The batsmen pick up a couple. End of another good over for the away side, 7 runs off it in the end. They are 1 shy of the three-figure mark now.
Length delivery on middle, the left-hander flicks it to mid-wicket.

Now Trent Boult is again having an issue with the landing spot. Also looks like something is stuck in his shoe. We see a slight depression on the landing area, tells us about the dampness of the surface.
On a good length and outside off, Mominul looks to cut but misses it due to the away movement on this one.
On a good length on off, Haque looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Another check for the shape of the ball. Goes through the hoops again. And once again, the umpire says it is fine and asks the bowler to continue...
On a good length on middle, Iqbal defends it towards the leg side for a run.

FOUR BYES! Bowls a quick bouncer outside off, Iqbal does well to duck under it. The ball goes towards the left and above Watling who tries to jump and catch it but it goes over him and to the rope. Boult looks really frustrated!
Full on off, Haque drives it to mid off.
Full and outside off, Mominul looks to drive but misses it due to the bounce on this one.
The umpire is checking the shape of the ball. Looks like it is fine. We will continue...
Length delivery on middle, Iqbal tucks it towards square leg for a run.
On a good length on off, Tamim defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Good shot. Full on middle, Iqbal flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

OUT! Gone at last! How many times have we seen a wicket fall after a break? De Grandhomme does the trick! A length ball on the off stump line from around the wicket, shapes away slight after landing off the seam. The ball takes the edge and carries to first slip where Taylor gobbles the ball up. The first and much-needed break for New Zealand. The 75-run stand comes to an end. A funny incident also happened during the wicket, the wicket-keeper suddenly runs to the left after the catch was taken seeing something go off Taylor's hand. He must have thought Ross had dropped the catch and that it was the ball but it was actually Rosco's finger guard. All smiles in the end for the Kiwis though.
Second consecutive leave for Tamim Iqbal. On a good length and outside off, Iqbal shoulders his arms to this one.

DRINKS BREAK - What a brilliant period of play for the visitors! Bangladesh's openers have not only gone wicketless in the first passage of cricket in this Test but also managed to score 74 runs in the 20 overs gone by. A healthy run rate of 3.7 to boot. On the other hand, the New Zealand pacers have not made much use of the conditions that were available to them, the surface did play better than expected but the consistency of the perfect line and length has been lacking. The hosts will look to break this partnership as soon as possible whereas the away side will look to continue the good work done so far. Thankfully, the rain has also stayed away so far. The home team is seen in a huddle during the break, before they head back to their positions. Post that, de Grandhomme gets some sawdust and drops it near the landing area.
Yorker to end the last over before Drinks, kept out well by Shadman.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg.

Perfect length from Matt, and on the middle stump line with some inward shape. Tamim gets inside the line and pushes it towards cover-point. The batsmen pick up a single. The throw from the fielder at the striker's end gets Shadman on the back side.

We are all set to begin at last. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Tamim Iqbal and Shadman Islam will open the batting for Bangladesh. Trent Boult will start the proceedings for New Zealand.

PITCH REPORT - The surface is green and it is grey overhead, says the pitch expert Mark Richardson. Hopefully, the rain will stay away he says and the game should happen without stoppages on Day 3. Coming to the wicket, he feels that it looks like a traditional Basin Reserve wicket. Informs us there is also some amount of moisture on the surface, which might make the ball hold up a bit. He moves on to the side of the pitch, where he feels more dampness. Reckons the swing could be easier to negotiate today more than tomorrow, when he feels could be toughest for batting. Signs off by saying that it is quite cold out there.

Mahmudullah, the Bangladesh captain says he would have liked to bowl first as well. Feels now they will have to bat well in the first session, forgetting the conditions and spend time in the middle, giving themselves a bit of chance. Informs us that the team has a couple of changes. Reckons they do not want to repeat the mistake of not being able to put a big first innings total on the board in the first Test.

Kane Williamson, the NZ skipper says that they need to bowl in the right areas. Informs they have a single change in the team, with Matt Henry coming in. Mentions that they will need to be a little more clinical in the way they go about their game.
TOSS - New Zealand won the coin flip and elected to bowl first.

After 2 days of just hope, we are finally primed for some action. BJ Watling was presented the match ball from the previous game for his record dismissals as wicket-keeper for New Zealand in Tests. The captains are now out in the middle for the toss with Scott Styris, the match referee and the mascot.
